html:
An Iron Age culture of the Baltic coast on the Sambia Peninsula and in Natangia, in what is now the Kaliningrad region of Russia. The map shows it in 1 BCE and 100 CE.

Its people were western Balts, ancestors of the Old Prussians of the Middle Ages, whose tribes included the Sambians and Natangians. They farmed and buried their dead in flat cemeteries, often with horses. Their wealth came from amber, which washes up on the Sambian shore in great amounts. In Roman times it travelled south along the Amber Road to the Roman Empire, and Roman coins and goods turn up in their graves. Tacitus describes amber gatherers on this coast, whom he calls the Aestii.
